message.content:
The sea usually looks **blue**—but its hue can shift all over the spectrum depending on conditions:

| Factor | Effect on Color |
|--------|----------------|
| **Depth & water composition** | Deeper waters absorb longer wavelengths (red/orange) more strongly, leaving shorter‑wavelength light (blue/green). Shallow, sandy bottoms reflect greenish tones. |
| **Clarity / suspended particles** | Clear water scatters less light → deeper blues. Turbid water reflects more white/lightness, giving a milky or brownish tint. |
| **Sun angle & time of day** | Early morning/evening sun gives warm reds/pinks; midday sun yields vivid azure. |
| **Algae/floating plants** | Greenish hues when phytoplankton blooms dominate. |
| **Ice/snow cover** | White or pale turquoise near polar regions. |

So while “blue” is the classic image, the actual color ranges from deep indigo to bright cyan, sometimes even green, gray, or brown, all influenced by those environmental factors.
